Couple Married in Newark Surrounded by Street Throng and Roughly Treated.
NEWARK, N. J., Aug. 4.—A negro and his white bride were given an unpleasant reception by a street crowd as they left the office of Justice of the Peace Bassett here, where they had just been married.

The couple were Carence Spain, a dapper colored man, twenty-eight years old, of Bloomfield, and Mary Stein, twenty-three, and pretty, who had been employed as a maid in a well-known family on Douglas Road, Glen Ridge.

They called on the justice last night, had the nuptial knot tied and were about to board a trolley car when somebody passed the word around that they were bride and bridegroom. Immediately a crowd gathered, jostled them, shouted and several times almost knocked them down.

As they boarded the car they were loudly leered.

Overseer Killed By Negro.
Memphis, August 13.—Edward Perry, a well-known overseer of a large plantation at Star Landing, Miss., thirty miles south of Memphis, was shot and killed today by a negro. While falling to the ground Perry drew a revolver and wounded his assailant. The negro made his escape. The negro had become boisterous and Perry attempted to pacify him. Perry was a brother of Police Captain Oliver H. Perry of Memphis.

Fruit For a Lynching.
Memphis, Tenn., Aug. 15.—Edward E. Perry, manager of the Elbass plantation, near Lake Cormorant, Miss., was murdered by a negro, Henry Young. If caught, it's 100 to 1 that he will be lynched.
henry-young-lake-cormorant-1905-08-16.A5:
NEGRO HANGED BY
MISSISSIPPI MOB
Confesses That He Killed Man, But Says the Shooting Was Accidental.
Memphis, August 16.—A Commercial- Appeal special from Lake Cormorant, Miss., says that Henry Young, the negro who shot and killed Edward E. Perry on the Bass plantation, near Lake Cormorant, last Sunday, was taken from Sheriff Withers and a deputy tonight and at the scene of his crime hanged by an armed mob. The negro confessed his guilt but pleaded that he did not intend to kill Perry, a pistol for which they were contending, he said, exploding in a scuffle. The mob numbered about 100 men.

Young was captured this morning while fording a river to reach his father's cabin on an island. Sheriff Winters, who with a posse of forty men had been scouring the country for the negro, was notified of the capture and took possession of the prisoned. Hastening with an armed escort around the negro to the town of Trenton, where he purposed taking a train for Hernando, the county seat, the Sheriff was confronted at the station by the mob, and before he could make an effort at resistance was overpowered and his prisoner taken from him. The mob then proceeded to the Bass plantation with Young and hanged him to a tree.
henry-young-lake-cormorant-1905-08-16.A15:
MURDER AND LYNCHING
E. H. Perry Shot to Death by Negro Whose Life Pays the Penalty.
The western portion of the county has been the scene of a good deal of excitement during the past few days, caused by the killing of a white man by a negro and the subsequent lynching of the murderer.

Edward E. Perry, manager for E. L. Bass, was the man who met his death, and Henry Young, a tenant of the place, did the shooting. The tradey took place early Sunday morning. The negro had been drinking and "raising a rough house" all Saturday night and ended up by shooting his wife, inflicting a flesh wound. He announced his determination to finish his job and Mr. Perry was summoned to prevent the negro from killing his wife. The white man went to the negroe's house for this purpose and the negro without warning fired upon him, inflicting a wound from which he soon died.

Sheriff Withers was notified of the killing and went to the scene at once. A posse was organized and bloodhounds secured and a determined search for the slayer was begun. It was not until Wednesday that the negro was located trying to make his way to Cat Island, near Penton, where his father lived. He was captured by a fisherman and the sheriff, who with his posse, was still searching for the murderer, was notified. Mr. Withers and Deputy Scott took charge of the prisoner and carried him to Penton, where they intended to catch the train. Meanwhile news of the

The work was done in a quiet manner and as soon as the negro was pronounced dead the mob dispersed.

Ferguson, claim agent of the Louisiana & Arkansas railroad, was killed near Stamps today by a negro named Ike Kinney. Kinney killed a negro this morning at Stamps and escaped, and Ferguson was a member of a posse which went in search of him. The negro was encountered about three miles from Stamps, and opened fire, killing Ferguson. A reward of $500 has been offered for Kinney, and special trains have been sent to Pine Bluff, Ark., to take bloodhounds to Stamps. SECY. WILSON EXPLAINS. Tells Why He Sent His Son to Alaska on Government Business.
Washington, Aug. 2.—Secy. Wilson today issued a statement relating to a charge that his son and private secretary, Jasper Wilson, made a trip to Alaska about a year ago at the expense of the department. Secy. Wilson says the trip was made at his instance and was for the purpose of ascertaining the condition of the game there, delegates from Alaska having protested against sending anybody in there with permission to shoot and bring out trophies. The miners claimed that they lived there in the winter; that the game was a resource which often stood between them and starvation.

"I wanted to know the real facts," said the secretary, "and sent my private secretary up there. He was a salaried officer here. The department paid his actual traveling expenses, of course. I send men all over the world for information.

"Upon receipt of my private secretary's report I shut down on the granting of permits to everybody excepting persons representing the museums and other educational institutions."

JEWS ABROAD.

Dr. Danziger Arrives to Give Dept. of Labor Information.

Washington, Aug. 2.—Dr. Adolphe Danziger, formerly United States consul at Madrid, arrived here today to lay before the department of commerce and labor memoranda concerning the condition of the Jews abroad, the information being gathered at the request of the department for use in the bureau of immigration in dealing with that class of immigrants. "In England, Germany and Russia," said Dr. Danziger, in reviewing his observations today, "what struck me most notably was the hopeful views the Jews take of America. "The people I met were hoping that the president would take the opportunity that presented itself to induce the Russian government to grant them freedom or at least to give them equal rights in Russia. BLOODY Record Made By a Bad Negro In Arkansas. HE HAD KILLED TWO PEOPLE AND WOUNDED FOUR OTHERS WHEN SHOT BY POSSE. PURSUED BY SPECIAL TRAIN.
Little Rock, Ark., Aug. 3.—A special from Lewisville, Ark., says:

After killing two persons, seriously and probably fatally shooting two others, one a woman, and less seriously shooting two more, Ike Kinney, a desperate negro, was killed in a river bottom at Doella, six miles south of Lewisville, at noon to-day, after a hot fight with a posse of citizens that had surrounded him. His bloody record for twenty-four hours is:

August 2 (morning), killed a negro at Stamps.

August 2 (afternoon), killed E. R. Ferguson, claim agent of the Louisiana and Arkansas railroad, member of a posse three miles from Stamps.

August 3 (3 a. m.), seriously shot Mrs. Stewart, of Greensburg, and Mr. Stewart, her husband.

August 3 (noon), shot Alvil Barham through the neck and shot a finger off one of C. F. Nash's hands.

**Left Trail of Gore.**

Kinney, who had killed a negro at Stamps on Wednesday, fled, and while being pursued by a posse shot and killed E. R. Ferguson. This augmented the feeling against the negro, but to cap the bloody climax, it was learned that a man named Stewart and his wife from Greensburg had been shot by Kinney at 3 o'clock this morning, three miles from Lewisville. Without a word of warning, the negro opened with his Winchester, firing four shots and shooting Mrs. Stewart through the breast and her husband through the side. Mrs. Stewart, who is now at Stamps, was seriously wounded. After shooting Mr. and Mrs. Stewart, the negro told them that he thought they were members of a posse, and assured them he was very sorry that he had fired on them.

Early this morning about twenty-five men with dogs started out on Kinney's trail. They got the first clew from a man on a river farm south of this city, who told them that a negro had come to his house that morning and asked for a drink of water and to be taken across Red river.

Killed By a Posse.

A few members of the searching party finally located Kinney in a bottom near Doella, which is a plantation post-office. Word was at once sent to Lewisville and a posse started shortly before noon on a special train for the scene of the expected battle.

As soon as the posse had arrived and begun to close in on the negro, he opened fire. C. F. Nash lost a finger. Alvin Barham was shot through the neck and seriously wounded. Then W. C. Nash shot a bullet in the negro and tumbled him over dead. The posse and the body of the negro were brought back to Stamps on a special train.

Fifteen hundred dollars had been offered for the capture of Kinney, dead or alive.

NEVER MISSED TEAM

LIVERYMAN RENTED RIG TO SALESMAN.

KEPT IT SIXTEEN MONTHS.

Bill Footed Up $485—Charged With Using Loaded Cane On His Brother.

Lexington, Ky., Aug. 3.—[Special.]—After keeping a horse and buggy which he had rented from G. H. Goodrich for sixteen months N. B. Duncan, a traveling salesman for the Magic Food Company, of Chattanooga, Tenn., drove up in front of the stable last night. Mr. Goodrich was unable to recognize the horse and vehicle as his and even declared that he had not missed either the animal or the rig. He said Duncan had been in the habit of renting rigs almost weekly from him, and just supposed that the last one rented had not been returned. Duncan explained that he had been all through the South with the horse and buggy, and both the animal and buggy bore proof to the statement. While Mr. Goodrich was surprised at the return of the rig. Duncan was equally surprised over the amount of the livery bill which Goodrich made out to him and which amounted to $485, or about three times the value of the horse and vehicle.

Funeral of Mrs. Gormley.

The body of Mrs. Margaret Gormley, of this city, who died suddenly in Cincinnati Wednesday morning, was brought here to-day and the funeral services will be held Friday morning at St. Paul's Catholic church. Mrs. Gormley was the mother of Miss Mamye Gormley, who returned yesterday from a trip to Europe, where she had been as the guest of a Cincinnati paper, having received the most votes in the contest for the most popular clerk of this city.

**Thrown From Her Buggy.**

Mrs. Stella Wood, living on the Mt. Liberty pike, was run into while driving on the road last night, her vehicle being upset, throwing her to the ground and dragging her some distance before the horse could be stopped. Mrs. Wood stated that she was run into by three drunken men who were driving along at a rapid gait and who never stopped to see if she was injured.

**Brother Swore Out Warrant.**

John H. Stamper, proprietor of a grocery on Georgetown street, was arrested this morning on a warrant sworn out by his brother, Asa Stamper, charging him with assault. The younger Stamper alleges that his brother struck him over the head with a loaded cane while they were trying to have a settlement. When Stamper appeared before Magistrate Oldham last night and asked for the warrant he was very weak from the blow and had to be taken home in a carriage.

IN DELIRIUM SAW AIRSHIP THEN SEVERED AN ARTERY.

Petersburg, Ind., Aug. 3.—[Special.]—While in a delirium to-day Alex. Amos imagined he saw an airship from which people were firing at him. He grabbed a butcher knife and severed an artery in his arm. He will die.

Richmond, Ky., Aug. 3.—[Special.]—John Ballard, assistant postmaster of the local post-office, was arrested last night by Secret Service men while in the act of rifling the United States mail. For about two months past small amounts have been missing from registered letters and in consequence of which Government detectives were detailed to investigate this shortage.

Last night young Ballard was seen to open several packages and secrete the contents on his person. He was promptly apprehended and brought before United States Commissioner W. C. Bennett, of this city, by whom he was released on $300 bond to await the action of the Federal grand jury in October.

The incident has created a sensation, as Mr. Ballard is a popular and prominent young man. He is a nephew of both Postmaster C. C. Wallace, of this city, and Bland Ballard, Chief Deputy in the Collector's office at Danville. The amount of his alleged pilferings total about $52.

BIGAMY IS CHARGED.

Jas. F. Hayden, Who Deserted Wife and Children In Louisville, Under Arrest.

Elizabethtown, Aug. 3.—[Special.]—Capt. W. C. Elliott, a well-known detective of this place, has just worked out a sensational case against James F. Hayden, formerly of Elizabethtown, and as a result Hayden is in jail at Selmer, Tenn., charged with bigamy. The preliminary trial is set for next Tuesday. Several years ago Hayden married a Miss Wiseman, of Hardin. It is now alleged that he deserted his wife and eight children in Louisville last October, going to Tennessee, where he was known as Frank Hayden. On March 16 of the current year he married Miss Kittie Perkins, of Stantonville, a graduate of Hamilton College, Lexington, Ky., and worth about $15,000. It is charged that Hayden, after trying vainly to get her fortune into his own hands, so conducted himself as to arouse suspicion, with the result that Detective Elliott was called in to investigate the case. While in Kentucky Hayden was a stock dealer and is well known in this and adjoining counties. Capt. Elliott and Mrs. Hayden, of Louisville, the prisoner's first wife, and from whom he has never been divorced, will attend the examining trial Tuesday as witnesses.

SAVED BY A CLOSE SHAVE
Alabama Sheriff Makes Prisoner Shave and Sends Him Safely Through a Mob.

Mobile, Ala., Aug. 4.—Brooks King was brought here from Monroeville, Ala., for safe keeping.

He owes his life to a close shave. King was convicted of murder and sentenced to 35 years at hard labor. A mob, on hearing the verdict, marched on the jail. Sheriff Saulberry meanwhile had made King shave himself clean, and handcuffed to a misdemeanor prisoner, marched his man through the crowd to the station. No one in the mob suspected the ruse.
